command:
git add README.md docs/README-extended.md "backlog/tasks/aprv-412 - README-split-short-README-plus-docs-README-extended.md.md" && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
APRV-412: name policy amend as the way to land a policy edit

The short README pointed a reader at the bare attest verb after a policy
change, and the guide never said what to do with an edited APPROVAL.md in
a checkout behind main. Both now name `approval policy amend` (with --pr
in a repository) and the guide says not to stash, reset or check the file
out to get past a refused sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin claude/aprv-412-amend-signpost && gh pr create --base main --head claude/aprv-412-amend-signpost --title "APRV-412: name policy amend as the way to land a policy edit" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Tasks: APRV-412 (follow-up)

The short README told a reader to run the bare `approval policy attest` after changing the policy, and the extended guide never said what to do when an edited `APPROVAL.md` sits in a checkout behind main (the `log-sync-git-failed` refusal). Both now name `approval policy amend`, with `--pr` in a repository, as the way to land a policy edit, and the guide says explicitly not to stash, reset or check the file out to get past a refused sync.

Docs only. docs-guard 17/17 locally.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
gh pr merge claude/aprv-412-amend-signpost --merge 2>&1 | tail -1
